Data.Recommendedapproach: Approve the draft if you are comfortable escalating the policy question, since it accurately avoids inventing a dual-boot answer not present in SupportKB. Route the ticket to the endpoint management or security review owner to confirm whether dual-boot Ubuntu and disk repartitioning are permitted for company laptops. Verify whether Ubuntu or any partitioning tool is already listed in Company Portal; if not, advise the requester to submit a Software Request with business justification per the KB software request article.
Data.Subject: Dual-boot Linux on company laptop for data science
Data.Body: Our data science group wants to dual-boot Ubuntu on HomeFix laptops for GPU workloads. Is dual-boot supported, and is there an approved disk-partitioning tool we should use?
Data.Rationale: This is a software policy/request question with no immediate work stoppage, so Low priority is appropriate. SupportKB covers approved software install/request policy and warns against open-internet installs, but it does not state whether dual-boot Ubuntu is supported or identify an approved partitioning tool.
Data.Draftreply:
Hi Viktor,

Thanks for checking before making changes to HomeFix laptops for the data science group.

I don’t have a published helpdesk article that confirms whether dual-boot Ubuntu is supported or names an approved disk-partitioning tool, so I’m routing this to the appropriate specialist team for review.

In the meantime, please do not install Ubuntu, disk-partitioning tools, or other software from the open internet on company laptops. HomeFix policy says approved software should be installed through Company Portal, and software not on the Approved list should be requested through the IT catalog with a business justification. Installs outside Company Portal are blocked by policy and generate a security alert.

We’ll follow up once the specialist team confirms the approved path for your GPU workload requirement.

Best regards,
HomeFix Supply Support Team
